newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela oil prices halt slide.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela oil prices halt slide.

text.p: The price of Venezuela's oil export basket rose by 65 cents during the week ending March 21 to stand at $17.60 per barrel on Friday, according to data released by Venezuela's Energy and Mines Ministry.
It was the first weekly rise in eight weeks and traders in New York attributed the change of trend to heavy buying on the futures markets by investment funds.
Also, low inventories of gasoline in the key U.S. market were a cause for concern, they added.

The average Venezuelan basket price for March so far was $17.05 per barrel, versus $16.89 last Friday. The February average was $18.78 and in January is reached $21.53 per barrel, one of the highest levels in recent years.
The average price for the year stood at $19.39 per barrel, 20 cents below last week, but still $1.00 above the 1996 average and about $4.50 above 1995.

Venezuela's government based its 1997 budget on an average price for the year of $14.00, although Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta has said he expects the price to stay above $15.50 per barrel.
